key_insight: Generative strength in unified multimodal models does not uniformly improve understanding; UniG2U-Bench pinpoints the specific regimes and subtasks where generation helps (or fails) by systematically testing 7 regimes and 30 subtasks.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a systematic evaluation framework that clarifies when and how generation-to-understanding (G2U) capabilities benefit multimodal understanding.
method: Design UniG2U-Bench: a taxonomy partitioning G2U evaluation into 7 regimes and 30 subtasks that span implicit and explicit visual transformations.
Construct task suites and controlled evaluation protocols to measure how generative components affect downstream understanding.
Evaluate unified multimodal models across the regimes to analyze performance patterns, benefits, and failure modes of generation-enabled understanding.
impact: Gives researchers and engineers a practical, fine-grained benchmark to decide when to rely on generative unified models versus specialized perception or reasoning modules; informs model design, ablation studies, and targeted improvements in multimodal systems.
visual_elements: Regime–subtask matrix heatmap showing where generation improves or degrades understanding across the 7 regimes × 30 subtasks.
Pipeline diagram: input image → (implicit/explicit) visual transformation → generative component → understanding output, highlighting points of influence.
Bar charts or radar plots comparing model performance by regime to reveal strengths and weaknesses of unified generative approaches.
Example input–output triplets illustrating implicit vs explicit visual transformations and corresponding understanding tasks.
paper_title: UniG2U-Bench: Do Unified Models Advance Multimodal Understanding?
paper_authors: Zimo Wen, Boxiu Li, Wanbo Zhang, Junxiang Lei, Xiaoyu Chen
